content:
sam: noticing a sudden P95 latency jump on cluster-gamma around 03:12 UTC, roughly +3x compared to baseline. traced to serving nodes behind gw-prod-14. anyone else seeing this?

maya: yep saw alerts. p95 moved 420ms -> ~1.3s across several model routes. Queues spiking and GPU utils dropping. looks like batching collapsed.

jon: putting initial profiler dump in thread. short read: kernel selection moved to slower path for a lot of requests (fallback to fp32 matmul). suspect heuristic mis-predicted sequence length distribution.

jon: profiler snippet:
```
# p95 timeline
2026-03-18T03:11:50Z p95=420ms gpu_util=34% kv_cache_hit=82%
2026-03-18T03:12:30Z p95=1.2s gpu_util=12% kv_cache_hit=14%  <-- regression point
```

leah: kv_cache_hit rate drop is huge. any signs of KV thrashing or large prefix writes?

sam: checking request patterns: tenant alpha-corp had a surge of calls that included streaming tool-calls with embedded long trace payloads. prompt lengths jumped and many > 8k tokens. might be evicting caches.

rishi: quick query of metrics: `sum(rate(requests_total{tenant="alpha-corp"}[1m]))` spiked x6 at 03:11. Also saw `kv_cache_evictions_total` increase two orders of magnitude on nodes 7-9.

maya: batching heuristic was recently tweaked to prioritize latency by aggressive sequence-length bucketing (PR 4823). That change moves variable-length sequences into smaller batches to avoid head-of-line blocking. but if a tenant pumps many long sequences it fragments batches and lowers occupancy.

jon: looks like two compounding effects:
1) long prompt spike from alpha-corp -> KV cache cold starts + heavy KV writes -> eviction flood
2) batching heuristic fragments GPU workload -> smaller matmuls -> underutilized kernels -> kernel selector chooses fallback kernels (less optimized) for many shapes

leah: infra-bot telemetry shows kernel_selector.log: several "fallback_to_generic" entries around 03:12. excerpt:
```
[03:12:21] kernel_selector: shape=(1,16384) heuristics failed -> fallback_to_generic_fp32
[03:12:22] kernel_selector: shape=(3,10240) heuristics failed -> fallback_to_generic_fp32
```

sam: that explains higher CPU and lower GPU util. also streaming backpressure on the ingress resulted in many open connections and inflight prefixes. stacked tool-calls were causing repeated re-requests while waiting for stream acks.

rishi: can we confirm if quantization path was disabled for these shapes? maybe selector avoided int8 kernels because sequence length outside training distribution.

jon: yes, selector logs show "quant_profile_mismatch" for a lot of requests. Quantization profiles are keyed by sequence_percentile heuristics; percentile estimation is stale under this sudden distribution shift.

maya: rollback option: revert the recent bucketing change (PR 4823) and increase KV cache capacity on affected nodes as short-term mitigation. also add an emergency routing rule to divert large requests to dedicated-capacity pool. thoughts?

leah: agree on emergency route. set a temporary limit for streaming tool-call concurrency per-tenant to reduce pressure. we should also throttle alpha-corp while we triage. pinging @ops to get tenant throttles.

sam: executed quick fix: added tenant throttle (alpha-corp) at 03:20 via admin CLI and enabled emergency route to dedicated-cap-02. immediate drop in kv_evictions and p95 started trending down.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: reverted batching-heuristic (PR 4823) -> staging -> canary -> prod. rollout started at 03:28, completed 03:34.

rishi: after rollback and throttle, metrics:
```
2026-03-18T03:35:00Z p95=480ms gpu_util=68% kv_cache_hit=79%
```

jon: next steps for follow-up:
- postmortem: root cause is correlated distribution shift + heuristic tuning that assumed stable seq-length percentiles
- immediate: add circuit-breaker on kernel-selector to avoid mass fallback when a shape storm appears
- medium: add online percentile estimator that adapts faster and surfaces distribution drift alerts
- long: per-tenant preflight checks for tool-calling loops and streaming backlog signals

maya: i'll open a ticket to add a KV cache slab metric per-tenant and alert when eviction_rate > 0.2x baseline. also capturing the alpha-corp request traces for an eval harness.

leah: include a sample of the offending request (redacted) so model team can reproduce stream/tool loop locally. also recommend a small guard in runtime to limit max prefix writes per connection.

sam: thanks all — follow-up meeting at 10:00 to draft the postmortem. tagging RACI: sam (incident lead), jon (runtime), rishi (infra), maya (heuristics), leah (ops). :white_check_mark:

maya: adding retro notes: 1) prefer conservative heuristics that fail open (no mass fallback), 2) prioritize quick telemetry that flags quota/sequence outliers, 3) per-tenant safety knobs.

jon: will attach the profiler tarball and kernel_selector logs to the incident ticket. command used to pull logs:
```
scp infra@gw-prod-14:/var/log/redwood/kernel_selector.log ./kernel_selector.03-12.tgz
```

sam: closing thread for now, will post the postmortem link once drafted. thanks for quick response. :pray:
